facts.claim: Median private B2B SaaS gross revenue retention fell to 84% in 2025 while annual net revenue retention compressed to 101%
facts.excerpt: The median SaaS gross revenue retention rate fell to 84% in 2025; annual NRR compressed to 101% across all private B2B SaaS.

facts.claim: Gross revenue retention by contract size runs 82% under 25,000 dollars ACV, 88% from 25,000 to 100,000, and 95% above
facts.excerpt: SMB (<$25K ACV): 82% GRR; Mid-Market ($25K-$100K): 88% GRR; Enterprise (>$100K ACV): 95% GRR.

facts.claim: Net revenue retention splits hard by contract size: 97% under 25,000 dollars ACV, about 108% from 25,000 to 100,000, and 118% above that
facts.excerpt: Enterprise (over $100K ACV) at a median 118% NRR, mid-market ($25K-$100K ACV) at about 108%, and SMB (under $25K ACV) at 97%.

facts.claim: Smart retry alone recovers about 40% of failed payments, a card updater 25%, and dunning email adds 15 to 20% on top
facts.excerpt: Smart retry alone recovers 40%, card updater 25%, and emails add 15-20% on top; combining all three reaches 70%.

facts.claim: The RBI E-Mandate Framework 2026 allows recurring debits up to 15,000 rupees without additional authentication, and up to 1,00,000 rupees for insurance, mutual funds and credit-card bills
facts.source_title: UPI Autopay and Recurring Payments: Compliance Checklist Under RBI's E-Mandate Framework 2026
facts.excerpt: Recurring transactions up to Rs 15,000 process without additional factor authentication after setup; insurance, mutual funds and card bills up to Rs 1,00,000.

facts.claim: India's 2021 card e-mandate rules pushed card subscription failure rates above 20% in some categories
facts.source_title: UPI Autopay vs Card e-Mandates: 2026 Decision Guide
facts.excerpt: The mandate requiring extra authentication for card payments above Rs 5,000 caused failure rates to spike to 20%+ in some categories, accelerating UPI Autopay adoption.
